r3_note: Names: Male (ماليه) = Malé, Amal = person - not words. 14:21-14:51 is one how-do-I-say 'on the Wi-Fi' exchange (A7); D5 sits inside it. 46:18-46:49 is one superlative-with-someone drill: D2 is the هذا/حدا word, A21 the -o ending.

rows.amal_said: شو يعني لسه الزباين يروحوا؟ ... لا، لا الزباين يروحوا. ... There are other words, but the one we know is لا.
rows.why: He used لسه (sheet: 'still / not yet | Lissa') for 'until'; Amal asked what it means and gave لا الزباين يروحوا ('the one we know is la'). Engine wrote 'divine' for الزباين.

rows.amal_said: واحد.
rows.chat: yoam el-5amees, wa7ad 3ashara alafain u sitte u 3eshreen
rows.why: For the date (the 1st) he started with feminine واحدة; Amal said واحد, and at 02:55 he states the rule he took from it: 'dates are واحد, times are واحدة'.
rows.r3_why: Voiced recast; his 02:55 remark confirms he registered a correction on the date number.

rows.amal_said: واحد. ... هيك الساعة واحدة.
rows.why: Clock time takes the feminine number; Amal echoed his واحد, he caught it ('times are واحدة') and she confirmed الساعة واحدة.

rows.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة، uh، أخ-أخ-أخضر أو،
rows.amal_said: بلوزة شو؟
rows.why: Feminine noun بلوزة needs the feminine colour; Amal prompted 'بلوزة شو؟' and he fixed to خضرا ('it's feminine').

rows.amal_said: Hafiz is a motivation، بس what's about motivated؟ ... متشـ... متشجع.
rows.why: Asked to recall yesterday's word 'motivated' he produced a different lexical item, حافز (sheet: 'motivation | 7aafez daafe3'; engine wrote حافظ); Amal said that is motivation and supplied متشجع (sheet: 'motivated | Mitshajje3'). He attempted a wrong word, so tier 1, not tier 0 didn't-know.
rows.r3_why: Tier 1: he gave a real but wrong word before saying he forgot; tier 0 is only for words never attempted.

rows.amal_said: هاي، هاي، برا، برا. ... مت-- Okay، شكرًا.
rows.why: He repeated her متشجع as مشجع (encourager / fan) at 06:36 and again at 07:36; after the second she started 'مت--' to restore the mit- form (sheet: 'motivated | Mitshajje3').

rows.medi_said: Is there a verb for حساب? Do you guys use it?
rows.amal_said: بحسب.
rows.why: He asked for the verb from حساب meaning 'to consider'; Amal supplied بحسب.

rows.amal_said: بس متشجع إله أو لا؟
rows.why: متشجع takes لـ - Amal herself modelled 'متشجع لـ العربي' and 'متشجع إله' right before; he dropped the preposition and she only fixed the word.

rows.medi_said: أنا في الـ Wi-Fi? Is that how you say it?
rows.amal_said: Yeah I'm on the wifi أنا عالـ wifi. ... على الـ، عالـ.
rows.why: 'On the wifi' takes على not في; he offered في and asked, Amal gave عالـ (and على الـ when he then dropped the el-).

rows.medi_said: So Shanteti, ... El Shogolelah El, uh, Amra.
rows.amal_said: Yes, but what's work bag without any my or yours?
rows.why: In idafa the owner ending goes on the last noun; Amal made him build 'work bag' first and he said 'Shantet Shogoli, not Shanteti Shogoli'.

rows.medi_said: So Shantet Shogoli, uh, uh, Amra.
rows.amal_said: That would mean is red. ... if it's possessed by a pronoun it's definitive, so the adjective after it should be definitive as well.
rows.why: An adjective after a definite (possessed) noun takes el-; without it the phrase becomes a sentence ('is red') - Amal said exactly that.

rows.medi_said: So would it be شنتت، شنتت شغلي الأحمر، الأحمر،
rows.amal_said: الحمرا.
rows.why: شنتة is feminine so the adjective is الحمرا; Amal recast and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: ما فيهن means there aren't here or there isn't here. ... Yeah, مشون.
rows.why: 'Not here' negates an adverb with مش, not ما في (there isn't); Amal explained his meaning and confirmed مش هون after he tried it.

rows.amal_said: ليش؟ لا، ليش. ... It's just اسم. Why would it be feminine?
rows.why: He added the feminine idafa -t to اسم, which is not feminine; Amal said لا, it's just اسم.
rows.english: the name of his old school

rows.amal_said: لا.
rows.why: The first word of idafa never takes el-; Amal said لا twice (29:57, 30:21).
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.medi_said: So الـ اسم قديم. No, it's like اسم القديمة. Okay, I don't know.
rows.amal_said: لا. [تضحك] لا. ... You just change the gender of Adeem.
rows.why: To make 'old' describe اسم the adjective must match اسم (masculine) - Amal: 'you just change the gender of adeem'.
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.amal_said: But her. Her favorite store. ... محل أواعيها المفضل
rows.why: He left out 'her'; Amal prompted 'But her' and gave محل أواعيها المفضل (possessive ending on the last noun).

rows.amal_said: صح. متأخر أو متأخرة. ... ليش؟
rows.why: طيارة is feminine; he offered masculine المتأخر, Amal prompted 'متأخر أو متأخرة', he switched to المتأخرة at 39:59 and she asked why (طيارة).
rows.r3_why: Her 'متأخر أو متأخرة' is a voiced prompt that got him to fix the gender.

rows.amal_said: No. Even though in English we say the, in Arabic we don't.
rows.why: Superlative أحسن + noun takes no el-; Amal said No and explained, he fixed to أحسن محل.

rows.amal_said: Mm, it works, yeah. هذا أحسن محل
rows.why: محل is masculine so it is هذا; Amal said 'it works' and modelled هذا أحسن محل without flagging هذي.

rows.medi_said: No, not-- أس-- أس-- أسوأ الزبون.
rows.amal_said: The worst.
rows.why: Superlative + noun takes no el- (her chat: aswa2 zboon); her voiced 'The worst.' is not a clear fix, so let pass. Repeated at 43:44.

rows.medi_said: Okay. So أحسن الزبون ما، ما تشتري إشي.
rows.why: Amal asked for 'the worst customer' and he had just said أسوأ; here he said أحسن (best) - may be a slip of the opposite word.

rows.medi_said: ما تشتري إشي. ما بتشتري. ما بتشتري.
rows.amal_said: It's ما بي، ما بيشتري because it's زبون.
rows.why: The verb must match زبون (he); he used the she/you form and Amal recast ما بيشتري 'because it's زبون'. (He fixed the b- himself.)

rows.amal_said: أكثر حدا بحبه.
rows.why: He used هذا (this) for 'someone' after she had just modelled أكثر حدا at 46:11; she recast أكثر حدا at 46:20 and again at 46:43 (sheet: 'someone | 7ada'); he only switched to حدا at 46:45.
rows.r3_why: Real wrong-word slip, recast twice; distinct from A21 (بحب -> بحبه).

rows.amal_said: بحبه.
rows.why: The verb needs the pointer ending back to حدا; Amal recast بحبه and he said 'There's a pointer'.
rows.english: the person I like the most

rows.amal_said: Why? ... بس if you say the week's beginning, now you'd have to be إضافة ... It would be the first week.
rows.why: He read her الأسبوع الأول as 'the week's beginning'; Amal asked why, explained that would need idafa with awal first, and confirmed it means the first week at 53:51.
rows.proposed_rule: awal before a noun (awal el-usboo3) = the beginning of; awal after a noun as an adjective (el-usboo3 el-awal) = the first - same as awal usboo3.
rows.r3_why: Real listening misread with a voiced fix; no bucket covers awal-as-tool vs awal-as-adjective (same rule as A22), so PROPOSE.

rows.medi_said: Il awal il tamreen or il tamreen il awal is the first exercise.
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. ... Of course.
rows.chat: awal laffe, awal el-lafe, el-laffe el-oola
rows.why: Amal had just taught that awal before the noun never takes el-; he said 'il awal il tamreen' and she let it pass with Mm-hmm. Latin-letter turn.
rows.proposed_rule: أول / تاني before a noun is a tool word and never takes el- (awal usboo3 = the first week; awal sayyaara); put after the noun it is an adjective and takes el- like the noun (el-usboo3 el-awal); awal + el-noun = the beginning of (awal el-usboo3).

rows.amal_said: Al laffa al oola. ... Al laffa, what does al laffa mean?
rows.chat: awal laffe, awal el-lafe, el-laffe el-oola
rows.why: Repeating her phrase he dropped el- on laffe; she repeated 'Al laffa al oola' until he got it.

rows.amal_said: Nafs al ishi. ... نفس إشي doesn't mean anything.
rows.why: Amal recast nafs al ishi and said نفس إشي without el- doesn't mean anything.
rows.proposed_rule: nafs (same) is a tool word before the noun and the noun after it takes el-: nafs el-ishi = the same thing; nafs ishi means nothing.
